Dilnaz, you asked how I lasted thirty years as a reporter without breaking. Let me tell you about my first big story.
I was twenty-five. A bus had gone into a canal near Ropar. I spent three days with the families. I came home and couldn't stop crying. For two weeks I ate standing up, slept in my clothes, read every report again and again.
My editor, an old man named Sethi, called me in. "Baljeet, you're drowning in their sorrow. That helps no one." He told me three things. Say: this is their grief, not mine. Step away from it every evening. And do one useful thing with it.
So I wrote a follow-up about the broken railing. It got fixed. And I started walking by the river each night without a notebook.
That's how I lasted. Not by feeling less. By carrying it differently.
